A split illustration contrasting Lyric and Narrative poetry. On the left side (Lyric): a person sitting thoughtfully by an open window looking up at a large moon, with musical notes floating around, expressing emotion. On the right side (Narrative): a sequence of actions shown in a scroll—a knight riding a horse, fighting a dragon, and returning to a castle, showing a story unfolding.

The Shakespearean side shows three blocks of 4 lines and a final block of 2 lines, with a bracket showing the rhyme scheme abab cdcd efef gg. The Petrarchan side shows a block of 8 lines and a block of 6 lines, with a bracket showing the rhyme scheme abbaabba cdecde. An arrow pointing to line 9 on the Petrarchan side and line 13 on the Shakespearean side is labeled 'Volta (the turn in thought)'.
